Growth mixture models (LCGA, GMM, parallel processes)

growth.Rd

Fits latent class growth analysis (LCGA) or a growth mixture model (GMM) to a repeated continuous measure, or to several measures jointly (parallel-process model).

Usage

growth(
  data,
  items,
  K,
  model = "lcga",
  times = NULL,
  degree = 1,
  processes = NULL,
  starts = c(100, 20),
  covariates = NULL,
  ref = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  seed = 20261119,
  maxiter = 5000,
  tol = 1e-10,
  cluster = NULL,
  strata = NULL,
  start = NULL,
  optseed = NULL
)

Arguments

data

Data frame or matrix (one row per respondent). Indicators may be factors, characters, logicals, labelled vectors or numeric category codes; NA marks a missing response.

items

Columns of the repeated measure, in time order (tidyselect). Not needed when processes is given.

K

Number of classes (a positive whole number).

model

"lcga" (default) or "gmm".

times

Time scores: a numeric vector with one value per wave, or a list of such vectors (one per process); default 0, 1, 2, ....

degree

Polynomial degree of the trajectories (1 = linear, 2 = quadratic), or a vector with one degree per process.

processes

Optional list of column selections, one per outcome, e.g. list(dep1:dep4, anx1:anx4), for a parallel-process model.

starts

Length-2 integer vector: number of stage-1 random starts and of stage-2 starts iterated to convergence (Mplus STARTS). A single number is recycled. The default c(100, 20) with 20 stage-1 EM iterations corresponds to Mplus STARTS = 100 20; STITERATIONS = 20 (the Mplus defaults are 20 4 and 10 iterations).

covariates

Optional numeric covariates for a one-step latent class regression (Mplus c ON x): columns of data (tidyselect, e.g. c(age, female)) or a numeric data frame / matrix with one row per row of data. Needs K >= 2.

ref

Reference class of the latent class regression (default: the last class).

weights

Optional sampling weights: one column of data (e.g. w) or a numeric vector with one value per row; rescaled to sum to the number of analysed rows.

seed

Random seed for the random starts.

maxiter

Maximum number of EM iterations in stage 2.

tol

Convergence tolerance: change in the log-likelihood per case.

cluster

Optional primary sampling units (PSUs) of a complex survey design (Mplus CLUSTER with TYPE = COMPLEX): one column of data (e.g. psu) or a vector with one value per row. Standard errors, the MLR scaling correction factor and the tests built on them (compare_models(), Wald tests of r3step(), bch(), dcat()) are then design-based: computed from PSU totals of the weighted scores. Estimates and the log-likelihood do not change. blrt() is not available (as in Mplus). Analysed rows may not have a missing value.

strata

Optional strata of the design (Mplus STRATIFICATION): one column of data or a vector. PSUs are nested in strata (equal cluster codes in different strata are different PSUs); without cluster every row is its own PSU. A stratum with a single PSU is kept, as in Mplus.

start

Optional start values: a fitted latentmix model of the same type and number of classes (for example a fit to other data, or with fewer random starts). EM then runs from its estimates only, without random starts (Mplus user starting values with STARTS = 0; the analogue of OUTPUT: SVALUES).

optseed

Optional start number: rerun only that random start (stage 1 and stage 2), the analogue of Mplus OPTSEED; see refit_start().

Value

An object of class latentmix (see lca()) with info$kind "LCGA" or "GMM" and the extra component processes (column names per process, or NULL).

Details

The selected columns are the waves of the repeated measure, in time order. Trajectories are polynomials of degree degree in the time scores times.

  • model = "lcga": latent class growth analysis (group-based trajectories; Nagin 1999); growth-factor variances fixed at zero (Mplus i s | y1@0 ...; i@0 s@0;).

  • model = "gmm": growth mixture model (Muthén & Shedden 1999): normally distributed growth factors within class, with a covariance matrix that is equal across classes (Mplus default).

Residual variances are wave-specific and equal across classes. Missing waves are handled by full-information maximum likelihood.

Parallel processes. processes = list(dep1:dep4, anx1:anx4) fits the trajectories of several outcomes jointly: each class has a trajectory for every outcome, and with "gmm" the growth factors of all outcomes are correlated within class (one joint covariance matrix). times and degree may then be given per process (a list of time vectors and a vector of degrees). items is not needed in that case.

Covariates, weights, complex survey designs (cluster, strata), standard errors and auxiliary models work as for lca(); growth models do not support known groups.

References

Muthén, B., & Shedden, K. (1999). Finite mixture modeling with mixture outcomes using the EM algorithm. Biometrics, 55(2), 463–469. doi:10.1111/j.0006-341X.1999.00463.x

Nagin, D. S. (1999). Analyzing developmental trajectories: A semiparametric, group-based approach. Psychological Methods, 4(2), 139–157. doi:10.1037/1082-989X.4.2.139

See also

growthparams(), parameters(), classify(), lm_table().

Examples

data(depression)
# \donttest{
# depressive symptoms (dep1-dep5, CES-D-10) at ages 12-16: which trajectories are there?
g <- growth(depression, dep1:dep5, K = 4, model = "gmm", degree = 2, times = 0:4)
#> Starting Julia ...
g
#> ━━ Growth mixture model ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
#>   4 profiles, 5 indicators, n = 600
#>   Trajectories: polynomial of degree 2 in times [0.0, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0]; residual variances wave-specific, equal across classes; growth factor covariance equal across classes
#>   Random starts: 100 / 20; best LL replicated 20 times
#> 
#> ── Fit ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

#>   Free parameters            26      BIC                   14503.184
#>   Observations              600      Sample-size adj. BIC  14420.641
#>   Best LL replicated    20 / 20      Entropy                   0.795
#>                                      Smallest class             9.5%
#> 
#> ── Class sizes ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#>   Class  Proportion  Modal n  Avg. posterior
#>   ──────────────────────────────────────────
#>   1           0.539      329           0.910

#>              intercept  linear  quadratic

#>   summary() for standard errors · lm_table() to export · classify() for posteriors
growthparams(g)$alpha   # intercept (age 12), slope, curvature: low stable, increasing,
#>                class1     class2     class3      class4
#> intercept  3.85175088  5.5588199 13.9719745 15.15416427
#> linear     0.42369154  2.1995717 -1.8708010  0.59139401
#> quadratic -0.01851857 -0.1323748  0.1070494  0.02189963
                        # decreasing and chronic-high classes, as generated
# parallel process: depression and anxiety share the trajectory classes (linear)
pp <- growth(depression, processes = list(dep1:dep5, anx1:anx5), K = 4, model = "gmm")
growthparams(pp)$psi    # within-class covariances, incl. depression-anxiety
